signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard shows a severe 1.310% weekly spread divergence, with JPY outperforming at +0.694% across 7 pairs while NZD anchors the laggard board at -0.616% across 4 pairs. NZD/USD trades at 0.5450, comfortably below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5567/0.5623/0.5795 in a confirmed downtrend. Fundamental backing for this gap is anchored by the Economic Surprise Index, where NZD registers a strong negative print of -15.4 while JPY sits in positive territory at +5.0. Options markets reflect extreme downside hedging with NZD/JPY fair-value z-score cheap at -2.28σ, while retail positioning is heavily crowded long at 95% for NZD/JPY, creating a massive capitulation threat. Despite a 2.75% RBNZ policy rate yielding a carry deficit against the Fed, NZD faces relentless multi-layer selling. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; severe G10 underperformance and negative ESI momentum dictate downside. Catalyst: BoJ Core CPI data release today. Risk: BoJ signals dovish policy continuity, compressing the G10 bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.01, maintaining a strong position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (158.69/158.04/158.88). The baseline is anchored by Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%, yielding a 275bp policy rate advantage for USD (+269bp on an OIS SOFR-TONIA basis). However, cross-asset correlations signal structural distortion, with USD/JPY vs VIX correlation breaking down to -0.063 (z=-2.29σ against the 252d norm of +0.271), showing JPY carry positioning is holding firm despite VIX elevating to 26.6. Saxo 25d Risk Reversals print a strong put skew of -1.87 with 1M IV at 7.7% vs HV30 at 5.5% (VRP +2.2%), indicating institutional desks are aggressively paying up for downside protection. CFTC COT data highlights JPY Leveraged Funds net short at -29,545 contracts (pctl 85, z +1.12), keeping crowded carry risks front and center as price trades near verbal intervention levels. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; structural carry advantage dominates while VIX remains contained below panic thresholds. Catalyst: US Core PCE and GDP updates on 24 Nov. Risk: BoJ/MoF intervention or VIX spike above 30 forces a sudden unwinding of crowded JPY shorts.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT Squeeze + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6629, extending below its SMA20/50/200 cluster of 0.6863/0.6953/0.7043 in a persistent technical downtrend. RBA sits at 4.85% (HIKING) vs Fed 4.00% (ON HOLD), providing an 85bp carry advantage for AUD (OIS SOFR vs AONIA spread at -93bp favoring AUD). Institutional and retail positioning present a sharp conflict: CFTC COT Leveraged Funds remain net long +26,143 contracts, but a massive weekly delta of -15,052 contracts pushes the 52-week percentile down to 19 (z -0.86), showing rapid institutional liquidation. Conversely, Retail sentiment data retail sentiment displays an extreme 88% long positioning (12% short), directly opposing the institutional net-unwind trend. Options markets confirm downside fear with 25d Risk Reversals printed at -1.60. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD; institutional liquidation and retail long crowding weigh on price despite the RBA rate advantage. Catalyst: Australia Construction Work Done data today. Risk: Rapid short covering triggered by a hawkish RBA policy surprise.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Retail Divergence + Technical Breakout
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4367, maintaining an uptrend above its SMA20/50/200 technical cluster (1.4158/1.4141/1.3932). The carry layer shows Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.50%, generating a +150bp yield spread that structurally supports USD. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds heavily short CAD with net -75,447 contracts (long% 22.5%), reflecting institutional alignment with the rate gap. A powerful divergence appears in retail sentiment, where Retail sentiment data shows traders are 93% short USD/CAD (7% long), fighting the prevailing directional trend as spot stretches toward multi-month highs. BEER fair value model marks USD/CAD rich at z=+2.23σ (fair value 1.4260), suggesting potential medium-term stretch, but immediate momentum remains supported by broad USD demand. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; structural carry advantage and extreme retail short fading support trend continuation. Catalyst: BoC Governor Macklem speech today. Risk: Sharp rebound in crude oil prices combined with hawkish BoC rhetoric.
